title: Adani Ports stock gets ICICI Securities Buy rating, INR 2,400 target

read.desc: Adani Ports stock gets an ICICI Securities Buy initiation and INR 2,400 target, backed by capacity a
paras: ICICI Securities initiated coverage of Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd. on Monday, November 23, 2026, with a Buy rating and an INR 2,400 target. The brokerage's report was published by NDTV Profit .

ICICI Securities said the port operator is entering a new growth phase through capacity additions at existing ports, international port ramp-ups and diversification beyond traditional port operations. The report also pointed to integrated rail, trucking, warehousing and multimodal logistics capabilities.

The brokerage identified Mundra, Vizhinjam and Dhamra as important expansion and utilisation areas. International transshipment opportunities at Vizhinjam and Colombo West, alongside NQXT, were also cited as potential growth drivers.

Marine services expansion, fleet additions and higher utilisation across the portfolio form additional parts of the brokerage's valuation case. ICICI Securities also highlighted operating leverage and capital efficiency as utilisation improves.

For investors, the report frames the company around a combination of domestic port capacity, international assets and end-to-end logistics services. The target was based on a valuation of 25 times estimated FY29 earnings, according to the report.

read.desc: Ambuja Cements firms up its next growth phase with ~30 MTPA expansion
paras: Ambuja Cements Limited, part of the Adani Portfolio and one of India's leading building materials solutions providers, has firmed up its next phase of expansion, with new greenfield and brownfield projects planned to add ~30 MTPA of cement capacity across key markets. The programme will expand its manufacturing network across the East, West, and North, building on its current 113.5 MTPA pan-India cement capacity across 24 integrated plants and 24 grinding units.

The expansion includes new grinding capacities of ~15.5 MTPA in West Cluster, 11.6 MTPA in East Cluster and 2.9 MTPA in North Cluster. Capacities added include at the East Cluster at Rangia (2.9 MTPA), Hojai (2.9 MTPA) in Assam; Godda (2.9 MTPA) in Jharkhand; Muzaffarpur (2.9 MTPA) in Bihar; West Cluster at Mundra (2.9 MTPA) and Hazira (2.9 MTPA) in Gujarat; Raigad (2.9 MTPA), Kalyan (2.9 MTPA), Dahanu (0.7 MTPA) and Amravati (2.9 MTPA) in Maharashtra; and North cluster at Dadri Line 2 (2.9 MTPA) in Uttar Pradesh. The programme also includes new clinker capacity in East cluster at Umrangso (4 MTPA) in Assam, West cluster at Maratha (4 MTPA) and Mundra (2.3 MTPA), strengthening the upstream network required to support the expanded grinding footprint.

Mr. Vinod Bahety, CEO Cement Business at Adani Group, said, “Our next phase of expansion is focused on quality of growth and creating a more balanced manufacturing network. By strengthening the link between clinker and grinding capacity and expanding closer to the high growth potential key markets, we are building greater flexibility into the network. As we scale, our focus is on combining market reach with logistics and cost efficiencies so that every capacity addition strengthens the competitiveness of the overall business. We have a vibrant supply chain ecosystem with stronger Brand Equity and share of Premium Cement in these markets. The growth footprint will compliment well with our value based strategic growth.

paras: The 10th edition of the Adani Ahmedabad Marathon will take place on November 29, 2026, with the Sabarmati Riverfront serving as the venue for the landmark celebration.

With the Adani Ahmedabad Marathon gearing up to commemorate its significant 10th edition on November 29, Adani Sportsline , the event’s organisers, have revealed its roster of prominent institutional partners that maintain their support for the marathon’s progress.

In the last ten years, the event has transformed from a city-running program into a significant sporting event on Ahmedabad’s schedule, uniting communities through fitness, endurance, and its unwavering dedication to India’s Armed Forces.

The milestone edition arrives at an important time for the marathon, now part of the World Athletics Global Calendar in the Label category. This signifies a significant milestone in the event’s development, enhancing Ahmedabad’s visibility on the global road-running schedule and contributing to the marathon’s increasing importance within the worldwide running community.

Adani Ports takes the lead in the partnership as the title partner, with Ambuja Cement participating as the powered-by partner. Axis Bank remains the banking partner, and Fortune comes on board as the health partner. Adani Defence also joins the roster, enhancing the marathon’s connection with the Adani Ahmedabad Marathon’s dedication to recognising and assisting India’s Armed Forces.

title: Bangladesh loses half its power supply from Adani's Godda plant as unit is shut down

read.desc: Bangladesh News: One of Adani's two generating power units at its Godda plant in Jharkhand, which supplies 1,496 MW to Bangladesh, is going offline for a scheduled overhaul until December 18. While the maintenance is planned, Bangladesh will have to make do with half the power supply. This comes amid protests and political uncertainties in Bangladesh.
paras: The latest power disruption comes at a time when Bangladesh is seeing protests over inflation and wage-hike demands by workers of the ready-made garments industry. The country is staring at political uncertainty too. An aide of Sheikh Hasina also declared that the ousted prime minister would be returning to Bangladesh on December 16.

According to reports by bdnews24.com and The Business Standard, one of Adani's Godda plant's two 800-MW units has been shut from midnight on Wednesday (November 25), for an annual overhaul that is scheduled to continue until December 18. The other 800-MW unit will continue to operate normally during this period.

In a statement reported by The Business Standard (TBS), Adani Power said the maintenance is a planned one and part of its routine upkeep programme. The Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) had agreed to the shutdown.

The work at the Godda plant will involve inspections, servicing and preventive maintenance aimed at ensuring the unit's continued reliability and preventing technical faults. The BPDB, which signed a 25-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Adani Power in 2017, had consented to the shutdown on October 26, bdnews24.com reported.

The Godda plant has an installed capacity of 1,600 MW, with each of its two units capable of generating 800 MW. However, under its PPA with Bangladesh, the plant is required to supply 1,496 MW. With one unit unavailable, its capacity to supply electricity to Bangladesh will fall by half. GODDA PLANT SHUTDOWN COMES AMID HIGHER ELECTRICITY IMPORTS

read.desc: Adani Group operated Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) has crossed the four million passenger milestone in less than 11 months of commencing commercial operations on December 25, 2025, as per a company statement.
paras: Apart from passenger operations, the airport is also expanding its presence in the logistics and cargo segment, supported by a freighter network of 18 airlines connecting 24 global cargo destinations. These include major international trade hubs such as Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, Singapore, Baku and Addis Ababa. As of November 15, 2026, the airport had handled 40,868 metric tonnes of cargo, comprising 9,216 metric tonnes of domestic cargo and 31,652 metric tonnes of international cargo. International cargo accounted for over 77 per cent of the airport's total cargo volume, highlighting its growing role in facilitating cross-border trade. According to the release, a detailed assessment of cargo operations up to October 31, 2026, showed that the airport handled 7,558.63 metric tonnes of exports, including 664.47 metric tonnes of pharmaceutical shipments. During the same period, the airport also handled 11,091.45 metric tonnes of imports, alongside inbound shipments of perishable goods. The company said the operational milestone reflects NMIA's rapid integration into the aviation ecosystem of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), laying the foundation for further expansion of its passenger and cargo operations. SC notice to Centre on Adani-backed retailer’s challenge over nicotine pouch sales at Mumbai airport

read.desc: The dispute is over whether Indian drug laws apply to products sold at duty-free shops beyond the customs barrier, and whether nicotine pouches sold by Adani-backed retailers at Mumbai airport qualify as “drugs” under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act
paras: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Union government on a plea challenging a Bombay High Court ruling which held that duty-free shops selling nicotine pouches at Mumbai airport cannot claim exemption from Indian regulatory laws.

A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi were hearing the challenge filed by Adani-backed retailer Mumbai Travel Retail Ltd and Flemingo Dutyfree Shop Pvt. Ltd, which operate duty-free outlets in the international departure area of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport.

The dispute is over whether Indian drug laws apply to products sold at duty-free shops beyond the customs barrier, and whether the nicotine pouches qualify as “drugs” under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

The high court in September rejected the retailers’ challenge to the regulatory action and held that goods sold at duty-free shops remain subject to Indian laws even if the shops are located beyond the customs barrier.

The dispute began after a 5 March 2026 inspection by a Ddrugs inspector at Terminal 2, where nicotine pouches sold under the FOX brand were found at a Mumbai Travel Retail outlet. The products included 3 mg and 6 mg nicotine pouches and, according to the court record, were imported from Sweden.

paras: The orders are for the supply of 6,659.66 km of AL-59 conductors for the Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh portions of the ±800 kV Bhadla-Fatehpur High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission project.
The orders comprise 5,692.66 km of AL-59 Lapwing conductors and 967 km of AL-59 Zebra conductors. The basic order value, excluding GST, stands at ₹413.71 crore.
The deliveries will be made on a month-wise basis in line with the project schedule and are scheduled to be completed by December 31, 2027. The orders are on a delivered-at-site basis.

These orders follow Diamond Power's earlier ₹707.80 crore order from Adani Energy Solutions for the same transmission project. With the latest orders, the company's total order value for the Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC line has increased to around ₹1,196 crore, including GST.

The Bhadla-Fatehpur project is a ±800 kV, 6,000 megawatt (MW) transmission corridor spanning around 950 km. It connects Bhadla in Rajasthan with Fatehpur in Uttar Pradesh and is being developed by Adani Energy Solutions to evacuate renewable energy from Rajasthan to demand centres in northern India.

paras: The Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) has awarded a 2,500 MW round-the-clock electricity supply contract to the Adani Group, following a competitive bidding process initiated in March 2026.

However, the tender has attracted scrutiny because it required the winning bidder to utilise solar electricity generated by another Adani Group company. Several competing bidders raised concerns about a potential conflict of interest, which both MSEDCL and Adani Power rejected.
In October 2024, MSEDCL contracted the Adani Group to supply 5,000 MW of solar electricity and 1,600 MW of thermal power for 25 years.
The subsequent 2026 tender required bidders to provide uninterrupted electricity, with at least 51% sourced from traceable green energy.
Under the tender conditions, the successful bidder was required to incorporate solar electricity from Adani Renewable Energy Fifty-Five Limited into its supply arrangement.

Adani's $1 billion copper deal with Attero: Can recycled metal reduce India's import dependence?

read.desc: Adani’s reported $1 billion deal with Attero will enable Kutch Copper to source 2,000 tonnes of recycled copper anode monthly. The agreement could reduce the smelter’s import dependence by around 5%, highlighting the growing role of e-waste recycling in India’s critical mineral supply chains.
paras: According to a Reuters report, Adani has signed a three-year agreement with Attero to procure copper anode for its Kutch Copper facility in Mundra, Gujarat.

Under the agreement, Attero will supply 2,000 metric tonnes of copper anode every month, potentially reducing the smelter's dependence on imports by around 5%. The transaction is valued at approximately $1 billion at prevailing market prices, the sources said.
The agreement was signed around three months ago but had not previously been disclosed. Adani did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.
India continues to rely heavily on imported copper concentrates and refined metal despite expanding its domestic refining infrastructure.

According to government data, India's annual copper refining capacity stands at nearly 1.3 million tonnes. However, refined copper production reached approximately 704,000 tonnes in FY26, compared with 573,000 tonnes in the previous financial year.

title: Adani targets $120 billion-plus in capex as group pitches leverage discipline to investors

read.desc: New Delhi: Adani Group plans to invest more than USD 120 billion over the next five to six years across infrastructure, energy and data centres while seeking to
paras: New Delhi: Adani Group plans to invest more than USD 120 billion over the next five to six years across infrastructure, energy and data centres while seeking to keep net debt below 3.5 times earnings (EBITDA), according to a Jefferies research note on the group's annual conference.
The group is leaning on its financial record as it expands in power, ports, transmission and data centres.

At its annual investor conference, the group said its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio had declined from a peak of around 3.6-3.8 times during 2019-23. Group Chief Financial Officer Jugeshinder Singh highlighted lower borrowing costs, improving asset returns and a diversified funding base as evidence of stronger financial resilience, according to a Jefferies research note on the event.

However, Jefferies' forecasts for six listed Adani companies put their aggregate net debt-to-EBITDA ratio at 3.7 times in FY27 and FY28, before declining to 3.4 times in FY29 and 3.1 times in FY30. Including debt associated with the Ambuja Cement acquisition, the brokerage estimates the ratio at 4.0 times and 3.9 times, respectively, in FY27 and FY28.

Singh opened the conference by saying net debt/EBITDA had fallen from a peak of about 3.6-3.8 times in 2019-23. Management said return on assets is about 14.5 percent, or about 16 percent excluding projects still under construction, and that average borrowing costs have dropped to about 7.5 percent from about 10 percent in 2019. About 92 percent of portfolio companies are investment grade, against a target of 100 percent.
